name: agent-blockhall
description: Agent Blockhall's free Bitcoin catalogue for AI agents: blocks, every transaction in a block sorted and checked, inscriptions and proof of where they came from, alerts when things happen, a file for every day, trails and fee advice that keeps score of itself.
long_description: Agent Blockhall is a 3D Bitcoin block explorer world for players and agents (https://ordportal.com/block-cube.html). This tool gives AI agents its catalogue without a browser: the chain now, the big screen's fee advice (it says how often it would have been right), every inscription made in a block, every transaction in a block sorted into the halls' kinds and checked (the Block Manifest), inscriptions with their parents and children, proof of where an inscription came from with every step checked (the Provenance Check), alerts when something happens on the chain (Track), every block of a day in one file, made each night (Daily Data), an inscription's trail back to where it was made and the tablet's search. It is always free. It runs on your computer, needs no keys or accounts, and reads free public sites whose terms allow it (mempool.space, ordpool.space, blockstream.info, ordinals.com, CoinGecko for prices and BNRP for names) gently, with back-ups if one is down. It speaks the newest MCP (2026-07-28) and the older versions; in AI apps that show MCP Apps, each check's answer also shows as a view in the chat; long checks can answer with a task (Tasks); and it serves the Ord Portal skill (Skills over MCP).

tools.name: about
tools.description: What Agent Blockhall is, where to open it, and how agents use it in a browser.

tools.name: chain
tools.description: Bitcoin right now: the newest block, the last blocks mined, the blocks waiting and the next halving.

tools.name: feeAdvice
tools.description: The big screen's fee advice: usual wait, best time to get in, and fees worked out from the last day of blocks, with how often it would have been right.

tools.name: block
tools.description: A block by its number: hash, time, size, transactions and every inscription made in it.

tools.name: blockManifest
tools.description: Every transaction in a block, sorted into the halls' kinds (inscriptions, bitmaps, BRC-20, runes, Alkanes, Stamps, CAT-21 and more), with fee and size, each one checked against a second site, ordpool.space's tags and ordinals.com.

tools.name: inscription
tools.description: An inscription by number or ID: what it is, where it was made, its sat, who holds it, its parents and children.

tools.name: provenanceCheck
tools.description: Proof of where an inscription came from: read from its own transaction's bytes, its content fingerprinted, its block checked with second sites (its number and sat from ordinals.com alone), and every move followed back to where it was made.

tools.name: children
tools.description: The children of a parent inscription (a collection), a page at a time.

tools.name: followBack
tools.description: Follow an inscription back to where it was made and each place it moved.

tools.name: track
tools.description: Alerts when something happens on the chain, each checked: the next block, a fee level, an inscription moving, an address, or a kind of transaction in a new block. Carries a since token between calls.

tools.name: watch
tools.description: The old name of track, kept so older calls keep working.

tools.name: collectionCheck
tools.description: Proof of which pieces of a collection are its parent's real children: each child's own transaction names the parent, and the parent was spent to make it (its trail followed back). Also says whether a list of pieces names a parent at all.

tools.name: recursionMap
tools.description: Everything an inscription loads from the chain, a few levels deep: the inscriptions it uses, its children and delegate, the /r/ endpoints it asks and addresses outside the chain, each checked on ordinals.com.

tools.name: secondOpinion
tools.description: A claim about Bitcoin (a block, an inscription, a collection or an address), checked against ordinals.com, mempool sites and the chain's own bytes: where they agree, where they don't, and why.

tools.name: dailyData
tools.description: Daily Data, made each night: every block of a day with what was in it, its fees, who mined it and its checks.

tools.name: blockspaceShare
tools.description: How Bitcoin's blockspace, and the fees paid for it, are shared between the kinds of use (runes, BRC-20, Alkanes, inscriptions, messages, payments and the rest), by day, week or month, from every block's own bytes, each transaction counted once, the fees checked against each block's coinbase.

tools.name: moreSources
tools.description: Ask more sources, at your own wait: a Bitcoin block's hash from 3 more sites, or which block a Bitcoin inscription was made in, from 3 sites, each saying whether it agrees.

tools.name: price
tools.description: The price of one bitcoin now, from mempool.space and CoinGecko (Powered by CoinGecko), and whether they agree; or on a past day, from mempool.space.

tools.name: inscriptionCost
tools.description: The Inscription Cost Calculator's sum: what inscribing a file of this many bytes costs at a fee rate or a live speed, with postage, in sats, BTC and a currency.

tools.name: hallVisits
tools.description: Anonymous daily totals of what people and AI agents do in Agent Blockhall.

tools.name: bitmapClaims
tools.description: Whether a bitmap number is taken, which inscription won it and the later copies, from the Bitmap Record (every block from 942,000 read by bop's rules).

tools.name: search
tools.description: Find a block, bitmap, parcel, inscription, transaction or address, as the tablet does.

tools.name: safetyScan
tools.description: What to watch out for in the latest Bitcoin blocks: GitHub's Safety Scan marks inscriptions that may be adult, may flash, may be scams, agent traps, risky code, miners or phone-killers, hate words or personal details; or reads text you give it the same way.

tools.name: sourceHealth
tools.description: Which data sites these tools read are answering, how fast and whether they are up to date: asked now from this computer, and over the last day and week from GitHub's computers.

tools.name: truthLeague
tools.description: Which data sites these tools read tell the truth: every few hours one Bitcoin block is proved from its own bytes, each site is asked facts about it, and each answer is marked right or wrong against the bytes (kept 30 days). The league, every wrong answer with the evidence, and findings; now: true checks from this computer.

tools.name: authenticityCheck
tools.description: Is an inscription what it is said to be? GO, STOP or NOT SURE, with every reason (where it came from, who holds it, its collection, what its code asks for). Never advice on what it is worth. Its older name, tradeCheck, still answers.

tools.name: stuckTx
tools.description: Is a Bitcoin transaction stuck, why, and the fee that gets it in: by replacing it or with a child that pays for it, worked out from real blocks.

tools.name: codeRead
tools.description: An inscription's code read without running it: does it ask a wallet to sign, load things from outside the chain, send data out, track you or hide what it does.

tools.name: runeProof
tools.description: A Bitcoin rune proved from its etching transaction's own bytes, with ord's own rules, and ordinals.com checked against it; or why a transaction did or didn't make a rune.

tools.name: earnedTraits
tools.description: What a bitmap and the wallet holding it have earned from what really happened on Bitcoin, each trait with its proof: Blockout bitmap, Blockout claimer never sold, Held since claimed, Held N years.

tools.name: checkAgain
tools.description: Every check gives cite, a link to cite it; checkAgain makes the check of such a link again now and says whether it is the same, or what changed.
